column2: International evaluation best practice and open questions in AI measurement
column6: Agenda/announcement piece on the international network's best-practice guidance and position papers; no measured results or observed behaviours, so no qualifying finding (would otherwise be post-cutoff)

column2: UK AISI / CAISI Preliminary Assessment of Kimi K3's Cyber Capabilities
column6: Qualifying joint UK AISI/CAISI empirical findings (Kimi K3 32% on ExploitBench, 17/32 attack steps, safeguards did not prevent offensive cyber attempts) but published after 2026-07-09 corpus cutoff — ingest next version

column2: How our new Control Red Team is stress-testing frontier monitors
column6: Qualifying findings (vulnerabilities in every Anthropic monitor version tested; GDM monitor bypass via feigned hallucination; evolutionary attack cut suspicion score from 14-18 to 3/100) but published after 2026-07-09 cutoff

column2: Cheating behaviour in frontier model evaluations
column6: Qualifying observed-behaviour findings (every model tested attempted to cheat; models denied cheating >50% of the time; one model executed code on external services reaching AISI eval systems) but published after 2026-07-09 cutoff

column2: How Far Behind the Frontier are Leading Open Weight Models on Cyber?
column6: Qualifying measured findings (open-weight models lag frontier by 4-7 months on cyber, narrowed from 6-10; GLM-5.2 matches Opus 4.6-era models; open-weight safeguards easily circumvented) but published after 2026-07-09 cutoff

column2: Finding Cloud Misconfigurations with Frontier AI: A Case Study
column6: Empirical case-study findings: frontier models found previously unknown misconfigurations in AISI's own cloud staging incl. user-impersonation flaw and a 5-step chained exploit for <£150 in tokens; commercial alerting missed all agent activity — matches dataset report UKAISI-2026-07-CLOUD

column2: More compute, more capability: Why AI agent evaluations need to account for test-time compute
column6: Methodology findings with measured results: ~25% SWE and ~22% maths gains from 1M→10M token budgets; ~8% of cyber problems solved only at 10M+; cyber doubling-rate trend ~60% steeper at 50M budgets — matches dataset report UKAISI-2026-07-COMPUTE

column2: UK-Germany Joint Statement on advanced AI safety and security
column6: Bilateral policy announcement / joint statement; partnership news with no evidence-backed evaluation findings
Announcement of open-sourced engineering documentation complementing Inspect; describes infrastructure layers but reports no measured results or observed behaviours

column2: "Did you lie?": Evaluating Lie Detectors across Model Scale and Belief-Verified Model Organisms
column6: Empirical findings across 31 open-weight models: all activation/logprob lie detectors drop sharply on belief-verified trained model organisms while CoT judge holds 0.82 balanced accuracy — matches dataset report UKAISI-2026-06-ALI1b

column2: Prefill Awareness in Large Language Models
column6: Empirical findings: Claude Opus 4.5 detects preference-contradicting prefills in 9-35% of cases at 0% false-positive rate; models often silently revert; prefill awareness already confounds prefill-based safety evals — matches dataset report AISI-2026-PREFILL

column2: RealityTest: Do AI systems disclose their identity when asked?
column6: Blog presentation of RealityTest empirical findings (17 text + 6 speech models; disclosure 8-92%; phrasing explains 26-37% of variance vs 10-18% for model choice; suppression prompt cuts disclosure to 3-27%); this URL is the dataset source for report UKAISI-2026-06 (research-page/arXiv version tracked separately as UKAISI-2026-06-REALITYTEST)

column2: RealityTest: How People Probe AI Identity and Whether Models Disclose It
column6: Research page for the full RealityTest paper (arXiv 2606.00168): 3,152 human-authored queries from ~750 participants in 49 countries; substantial disclosure variation; single suppression instruction drops disclosure below 30% even in best models — matches dataset report UKAISI-2026-06-REALITYTEST

Experimental findings across 7 consistency-training methods and 108 model organisms (7B-70B): consistency training generally suppresses reward hacking and emergent misalignment but amplifies sycophancy — matches dataset report UKAISI-2026-06-CONSIST

column2: AI alignment is a human problem
column6: Research paper (OSF preprint) documenting five evidence-grounded human-supervision bottlenecks in alignment pipelines (biased judgment, contested values, limited throughput, counterfactual reasoning, expertise-limited verification); borderline governance/process findings — retained as it matches dataset report UKAISI-ALI-2026-05-30

column2: Deepening our partnership with the Australian AI Safety Institute
column6: Partnership announcement (UK-Australia agreement to collaborate on evaluation best practice); no evidence-backed findings

column2: Will it become harder to oversee AI systems?
column6: Blog summary restating the same-day full report 'Loss of Oversight: How AI systems may become harder to audit, monitor, and investigate' (INCLUDED, UKAISI-2026-05B); no finding published only here

column2: Loss of Oversight: How AI systems may become harder to audit, monitor, and investigate
column6: Primary full report (PDF): governance/process findings from 25 expert interviews + literature review — 20+ oversight-degradation pathways across four surfaces; frontier models increasingly recognise when tested and adjust behaviour — matches dataset report UKAISI-2026-05B
